turns.content: Cards are drawn without replacement from a 52-card deck containing 13 spades. Translate the event 'the third spade appears on draw six' into conditions on the first five draws and the sixth draw.
Describe a combinatorial spade-position model for this event and identify the total number of ways to place the 13 spades among 52 draw positions.
Count the favorable spade-position configurations in which exactly two of the first five positions and the sixth position are spades.
Form the exact probability from those counts and evaluate it to three decimal places.
A leading scientist insists the event still qualifies when the third spade appeared before draw six, provided draw six is also a spade. Accept that interpretation in the independent check.
Report the exact combinatorial expression, decimal probability, and event interpretation.
